Ka'Bandha.wikitext:
{{KhornePortal}} '''Ka'Bandha''' is an [[Exalted Bloodthirster]] and one of the mightiest of [[Khorne]]'s servants.{{Fn|8}} {{Character |Portal ={{KhornePortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =KaBandha_EE_LE.jpg |Caption ={{PAGENAME}} |Title =[[Sanguinius|Angel's]] Bane{{Fn|10}}
Bane of the [[Blood Angels|Ninth Bloodline]]{{Fn|10}} |Homeworld = |Birth = |Active Period = |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Daemon]] |Type =[[Exalted Bloodthirster]] |Gender =Male |Relatives = |Occupation =Champion of [[Khorne]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Chaos]] **[[Khorne]] |Notes = }} ==History== ===Heresy-era=== ====Battle of Signus Prime==== Ka'Bandha first appeared leading Daemonic forces against the [[Blood Angels]] at the [[Battle of Signus Prime]] alongside the [[Keeper of Secrets]] [[Kyriss the Perverse]], being summoned to the [[Materium]] by sacrificing the [[Word Bearer]] [[Astropath]] [[Corocoro Sahzë]]. During the battle Ka'Bandha engaged in an airborne battle with [[Sanguinius]] and broke the Primarch's legs before unleashing the [[Ragefire]] upon the Legion and activating the dormant [[Red Thirst]] within the Legion. After Sanguinius was recovered thanks to the efforts of his Blood Angels, he engaged in a second round of fighting with Ka'Bandha and banished him back to the Warp.{{Fn|1a}} [[Image:Fear to Tread clean.jpg|thumb|right|330px|[[Sanguinius]] battles [[Ka'Bandha]] at Signus Prime{{Fn|5}}]] The brutal violence of Ka’bandha had unleashed a thirst for blood within the psyche of the [[Blood Angels]], that would not rest until every taint of [[Chaos]] had been erased from the planet,{{Fn|1b}} and which would later be known as the [[Red Thirst]]. ====The Challenge of Khorne==== Upon his return to the Warp, the broken Ka'Bandha crawled before [[Khorne]], met only with disgust and mockery. For his failure he was banished from Khorne's court, doomed to scavenge on weak souls to survive in the [[Formless Wastes]]. Other Bloodthirsters led hunting parties to seek his skull, and in time the desperate Ka'Bandha learned to be cunning. The hunters became the hunted, and Ka'Bandha took their armor and weapons for his own. Ka'Bandha eventually returned to the Fortress of Khorne with the skulls of these defeated foes, demanding a second chance from the Blood God. Khorne agreed, ordering Ka'Bandha to harvest 500 Blood Angels souls in the presence of Sanguinius.{{Fn|10}} He was later among the [[Greater Daemon]]s summoned into [[Realspace]] by the [[Thousand Sons]] during the [[Battle for Terra]].{{Fn|9a}} After the [[Lion's Gate Spaceport]] fell to the [[Traitor]]s, the Daemons were unleashed to destroy the [[Imperial Palace]]'s [[Colossi Gate]].{{Fn|9b}} While they succeeded in tearing down the Gate's outer defenses, the Daemons were destroyed by the [[White Scars]]' [[Stormseers]] and the [[Adeptus Custodes]], before they could complete their task.{{Fn|9c}} ====Siege of Terra==== Ka'Bandha would return once more to plague the [[Blood Angels]] during the last phase of the Siege of Terra. He was the first Greater Daemon who managed to pass the [[Emperor]]'s weakened psychic shield around the [[Sanctum Imperialis]], and attacked the [[Eternity Gate (Imperial)|Eternity Gate]]. There, he attempted to complete the mission Khorne had given him: Kill 500 Blood Angels in a set time in presence of Sanguinius. After breaking through the last Imperial defenses in front of the Eternity Gate, thus paving the way for the last grand Traitor assault (though he did not care for their success or failure), the Greater Daemon sought out Blood Angels among the defenders and butchered them. Sanguinius intervened, and the two duelled, though Ka'Bandha constantly attempted to break away to keep killing regular Blood Angels. Eventually, however, the Primarch managed to enrage him so much that he focused on their duel.{{Fn|10}} At one point, the Daemon cast Sanguinius to the ground. But, unlike Signus Prime, this time Sanguinius rose to his feet once again, and calling upon the last of his strength, hefted the Daemon by the neck. The Primarch was eventually able to break the Bloodthirster's back with the hilt of his sword. Afterwards the Primarch hurled the Greater Daemon back into the [[Heretic]] army and finally retreated back to the safety beyond the walls of the Eternity Gate.{{Fn|1d}}{{Fn|10}} Ka'Bandha's broken body was then consumed by weaker Khornate Daemons; later, Ka'bandha furiously realized that he had failed the test set by Khorne.{{Fn|10}} ===Post-Heresy=== [[Image:Ka'Bandha2.jpg|Ka'Bandha|thumb|right|330px|'''Ka'Bandha''' armed with the whip he used to crush Sanguinius' legs.]] The first [[Grey Knight]] to defeat Ka'Bandha was Brother-Captain [[Solor]]. To this day, Solor's bones have great sway over the Daemon. With the use of a sharpened femur the Grey Knights and Blood Angels were able to defeat Ka'Bandha in 944.M41.{{Fn|3}} In 823.[[M41]], Ka'Bandha slew Captain [[Abel Zorael]] in the [[Battle of Khartas]]. The [[Sanguinor]] intervened to banish the Daemon, but only after 80% of the Blood Angels had perished.{{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|2c}} In 944.M41 the Grey Knight's [[prognosticar]]s predicted that Ka’Bandha would shortly return to the mortal world. Knowing Ka'Bandha to be a dangerous foe, and moreover one who had earned the bitter enmity of the Blood Angels, the Grey Knights brought this news to the attention of [[Commander Dante]] and proposed a joint strike. A combined strike force of Blood Angels and Grey Knights assailed Ka'Bandha's fortress on the [[Daemon world]] of [[Kalagazaar]]. Ka'Bandha was banished, the Daemon armies were destroyed and Kalagazaar itself subjected to [[Exterminatus]]. At the campaign's end, the surviving Blood Angels had their memories wiped - a price Dante agreed with the Grey Knights at the mission's start.{{Fn|3}} In 999.M41, as the Blood Angels prepared for the main tendril of [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]] to [[Devastation of Baal|assault the Baal System]], [[Mephiston]] received portents that Ka'Bandha was preparing to assault the Chapter's home world where all the [[Chapters of the Blood]] had gathered.{{Fn|11a}} The presence of the Angel's Bane would throw the defense into chaos, and so Mephiston led a collection of [[Librarian]]s from various Chapters to thwart the Daemon's arrival. Though they managed to wound Ka'Bandha, they could not prevent his entry into the material realm.{{Fn|11b}} As the [[Great Rift]] tore through the Galaxy, he emerged above [[Baal Primus]], just short of his goal of Baal. Landing on the moon, he and his Daemons slaughtered Tyranids and Space Marines alike in a frenzied three-way slaughter.{{Fn|11c}} On Baal, as the Blood Angels finally defeated the last of the Tyranids, they could see Ka'Bandha's rune stretched across Baal Primus' southern hemisphere, written with the skulls of millions of Tyranid beasts. The monument was demolished from orbit by the fleets of the Blood Angel Chapters.{{Fn|11d}} Ka'Bandha next appeared during Khorne's [[Blood Crusade]], leading its second wave.{{Fn|6}} He was later banished back to the [[Warp]] by [[Mortarion]] during the [[War in the Rift]].{{Fn|7}} ==Images== Ka'Bandha1.jpg|[[Ka'Bandha]]{{Fn|1c}} Kabanda2022.jpg|Ka'Bandha resin miniature (2022) ==Trivia== {{Trivia}} Ka'Bandha is likely named after [[Wikipedia:Khabanda|Khabanda]], a demon from Hindu mythology. ===Conflicting sources=== In the [[Codex: Blood Angels (5th Edition)|5th edition Codex: Blood Angles]], Ka'Bandha is described as striking [[Ammonai]], the outermost planet of the [[Baal System]], as Hive Fleet Leviathan descends on the system.{{Fn|2b}} However in ''[[The Devastation of Baal (Novel)|The Devastation of Baal]]'', Ka'Bandha arrives above [[Baal Primus]] in the midst of the battle.{{Fn|11c}} ==Related videos== {{#evt: service=youtube |id=https://youtu.be/pWJjiVl_dJ8 |alignment=center |container=frame }} ==See Also== * [https://whfb.lexicanum.com/wiki/Ka%27Bandha Ka'Bandha in the Warhammer World] ==Sources== *1: [[Horus Heresy: Collected Visions]] **{{Endn|1a}}: pg. 177 **{{Endn|1b}}: pg. 340 **{{Endn|1c}}: pg. 341 **{{Endn|1d}}: pg. 359 *2: [[Codex: Blood Angels (5th Edition)]] **{{Endn|2a}}: pg. 14 **{{Endn|2b}}: pg. 17 **{{Endn|2c}}: pg. 18-19 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Warhammer 40,000 7th Edition Rulebook]] (E-Book) — ''Time of Ending'' *{{Endn|4}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Eight - ("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation =[[Moritat|Moritat Prime]] of the [[Raven Guard]]'s 14th Interdiction Company |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Raven Guard]] |Notes = }} '''Kaedes Nex''', also known as the '''Raven's Huntsman''' and '''Blood Crow''', was a [[Moritat]]-Prime of the [[Raven Guard]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]'s [[14th Interdiction Company (Raven Guard Legion)|14th Interdiction Company]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]]. He was known for his macabre obsession with the hunt.{{Fn|1}} ===Biography=== A dark figure among the kin who followed [[Corax]] from [[Deliverance]], Kaedes is seen as an ill-omen by his brothers. On [[Kiavahr]] in his youth he was known as ''Blood Crow'', an infamous murderer condemned to prison. There he remained, until Corax offered him a pardon if he fought alongside him. After enduring a painful transformation into a [[Space Marine]], only through the favor shown to him by Corax was he able to overcome the disdain of his fellow legionaries and rise through the ranks. In the grim shadow-wars fought by the Raven Guard, his murder-honed skills were employed with grim regularity.{{Fn|1}} When the Raven Guard came to [[Isstvan V]], Kaedes was among them but vanished into the wastes to stalk traitors on his own terms.{{Fn|1}} He was thought dead, but later reappeared on [[Mars]] during the [[Perditum Incursion]] to aid his Legion and Primarch in their escape from the Traitor-occupied world.{{Fn|3}} Kaedes was next reported to be part of the [[Shattered Legions]] warbands present at the [[Siege of Cthonia]].{{Fn|2}} ===Wargear=== Nex wielded a pair of [[Fulcrum Hand Cannon]]s.{{Fn|4}} ===Images=== [[Image:KaedesNexMini.jpg|thumb|center|190px|Kaedes Nex Miniature{{Fn|4}}]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Three - Extermination]], pg. 280 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Campaigns of the Age of Darkness: The Siege of Cthonia]], pg. 32 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Campaigns of the Age of Darkness: The Martian Civil War]], pgs. 42-43 *{{Endn|4}}: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250228055331/https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/wj9xgot4/heresy-thursday-the-blood-crow-is-on-the-hunt/ Warhammer Community: Heresy Thursday – The Blood Crow is on the hunt (posted 27/2/2025)] saved page, original link: https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/wj9xgot4/heresy-thursday-the-blood-crow-is-on-the-hunt/ (last accessed 28/2/2025) {{DEFAULTSORT:Nex, Kaedes}} [[Category:Characters (Great Crusade)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Raven Guard)]] [[fr:Kaedes Nex]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was an [[Oblivion Knight]]{{fn|1b}} of the [[Steel Foxes Cadre]] of the [[Sisters of Silence]] during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1d}}

===History===
During the [[War Within the Webway]] Kaeria was paired with the [[Custodian]] [[Diocletian Coros]] and the two grew into close comrades. Coros could understand Kaeria's meaning by simple facial expression and she did not have to sign to communicate with him. As a result, she accompanied Diocletian outside the [[Webway]] as they attempted to recruit reinforcements for the secret war.{{Fn|1a}} Later Kaeria oversaw the implementation of the '''Unspoken Sanction''' within the [[Imperial Palace]], sacrificing a thousand captured [[Psyker]]s to the [[Golden Throne]] so the [[Emperor]] could leave it for a single day.{{Fn|1c}}

Later during the [[Siege of Terra]], {{PAGENAME}} was one of those chosen to come before [[Malcador the Sigillite]] before he ascended the [[Golden Throne]] and carry out his final tasks given to them. She then gathered captive [[Psyker]]s to sacrifice to the Throne to aid Malcador in his struggle to power the ancient device.{{Fn|2}}

Kaeria died sometime later during the Siege. After the Heresy her tomb was destroyed by religious zealots that had deemed the [[Blank|soulless]] Sisters of Silence heretical. [[Diocletian Coros]] managed to track down her stolen sword to a black market to bury it in a new grave.{{Fn|3}}

Kage.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
[[Lieutenant (Imperial Guard)|Lieutenant]] '''Kage''' is an officer of the [[13th Penal Legion]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
Kage is notable for being the only member to have entered the 13th Penal Legion ''thrice''—conscripted in initially due to shooting his sergeant over a woman,{{Fn|2a}} being pardoned after completing the mission,{{Fn|2b}} then subsequently arrested once more for a second murder,{{Fn|3a}} falling to his assumed death,{{Fn|1}} and finally voluntarily placing himself under Colonel [[Schaeffer]]'s command indefinitely.{{Fn|4}}

During his time in the so-called ''"Last Chancers"'', Kage became the senior ranked penal officer, was assigned training and administrative duties as well as field leadership, and took part in several extremely hazardous missions. A latent [[psyker]] of minor ability, he was once believed to have become possessed by a [[daemonic]] entity during a mission to the world of [[Armageddon]], and to have perished falling into lava—though in the process ensuring the doom of the traitorous [[Imperial Commander|Overlord]] [[Herman von Strab]].{{Fn|1}} He was later found to have survived, crediting his survival and lack of subsequent possession to [[the Emperor]], and later rejoined Colonel Schaeffer's command to save Armageddon from daemonic incursion.{{Fn|4}}

Kai (Fallen Angel).wikitext:
{{DarkAngelsPortal}}
'''Kai''' is a [[Fallen Angel]] who was born on [[Caliban]]{{Fn|1b}} and is among those who now loyally serve their returned [[Primarch]], [[Lion El'Jonson]]{{Fn|1c}} as the [[Risen (The Fallen)|Risen]].{{Fn|1d}}
==History==
Before [[Destruction of Caliban|Caliban's destruction]] Kai held the rank of [[Lord Commander|Knight-Commander]] and was a skilled duelist. He believed himself to be the best swordsman in his [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], but other [[Dark Angels]] viewed him as a braggart and some even stated Kai's attitude made him a better fit for the [[Emperor's Children]]. However they also knew he was a warrior, who would never ask others to do what he would not. Millennia after his [[Adeptus Astartes Homeworld|Homeworld]]'s destruction, Kai emerged into [[Realspace]] and eventually met with his fellow Fallen, [[Aphkar]] and the two later met [[Lohoc]]. The three then banded together to survive in this new [[Imperium]], where the Fallen were hunted by the Dark Angels [[Chapter]] and the [[Unforgiven]]{{Fn|1c}}. Sometime after the [[Great Rift]]'s creation, they used a landing craft to travel to the [[Imperial]] world [[Avalus]] and crashed into its capital '''Xerxe'''. The three survived the crash and hid themselves shortly afterwards. They then began discreetly leaving symbols that were only understood by the Fallen and which pointed to the building they hid themselves in.{{Fn|1b}} 

The three later began hearing that their [[Primarch]], [[Lion El'Jonson]], had returned to the [[Imperium]] and was now in '''Xerxe'''. This was soon proven true, when the [[Fallen]] [[Zabriel]] found their hideout and stated he had been sent by the Primarch to find and recruit the Fallen{{Fn|1b}}, that El'Jonson believed resided in the Capital{{Fn|1a}}. The Primarch wished for them to fight by his side to defend the embattled [[Imperium]] and was willingly to put their differences behind them. This came about after El'Jonson met Zabriel and then learned that some of the Fallen honestly believed he had attacked them first, during the civil war on Caliban. After hearing this, Kai and [[Aphkar]] were against aiding their Primarch, as they thought El'Jonson was responsible for the civil war and the deaths of their brethren. However both were surprised when [[Lohoc]] agreed to serve his Primarch, without a second thought, as he had never believed El'Jonson had been responsible for the civil war. To him, Caliban was a strange world and had likely twisted [[Luther]]'s Dark Angels into causing the conflict. Kai agreed that something had seemed off with Luther and decided to meet with his Primarch, though he made sure to tell Zabriel that did not mean he would agree to El'Jonson's request. Aphkar reluctantly agreed to join them{{Fn|1b}} and Zabriel led the three to meet with their Primarch. The meeting began poorly, however, as Aphkar still held lots of anger towards their Primarch. Kai then took things a step further by activating his [[power sword]] and stating that if El'Jonson wanted his aid, then the Primarch would have to defeat him in a duel. While Kai had earlier mocked El'Jonson's aged appearance and wondered if his battle skills had now declined, the Primarch was able to easily defeat the swordsman. This led Kai to vow that he would serve El'Jonson, and both Aphkar and Lohoc agreed to do so as well.{{Fn|1c}}

'''Fateweaver''', the '''Oracle of Tzeentch''' originally known as '''Kairos''', is the personal Vizier of [[Tzeentch]] - a [[Lord of Change]] capable of seeing things hidden even from the gaze of its master.{{fn|1}} It is numbered among the [[Conclave Diabolus]], the hundred and one [[daemon]]s the [[Grey Knights]] consider most dangerous.{{Fn|5}}

===History===
Although Tzeentch could see all of the past and present, he was unable to grasp all of the uncountable threads of the future.  The need to overcome this one weakness took Tzeentch to the mystic [[Well of Eternity]] at the very centre of reality, where space and time originate and end.  However, even Tzeentch was afraid to enter the roiling currents of the well; so instead he sent his [[Lords of Change]], but none of them ever returned.  Finally, Tzeentch grabbed his vizir Kairos and cast him into the well.  This time, Kairos survived, just.  But when he resurfaced, Kairos was unnaturally aged, hunched and wizened.  His mighty pinions were reduced to feeble vestigial remains, and he now had two heads.  Henceforth, Kairos held both the knowledge of the future and the resulting insanity, and sits at Tzeentch's right side as his Oracle.  He is constantly mumbling madly, and suddenly bursting into rambling tirades about events still to happen.  Eighty-one Lords of Change are tasked with recording every word of the Oracle. A few mighty individuals, mortal and Daemon alike, are granted an audience with the Oracle for the completion of the most challenging of tasks for Tzeentch.  The Oracle knows the answer to all questions; but only one head will always answer the truth, while the other simultaneously delivers a contradictory answer, which is false but equally believable.  The resulting riddle invariably leaves the petitioner baffled.{{Fn|1}}

On the rare occasion that Tzeentch sends Kairos to the mortal battlefield, he is known as Fateweaver. He and his daemonic bodyguards are truly unstoppable, for he is able to use his great magical power and incredible prescience to influence the course of the battle.  However, if any unexpected harm comes to him, Kairos often retreats back to the Warp, afraid that his treacherous master might have intentionally hid that future from him.{{Fn|1}} 

====Great Crusade and Horus Heresy====
Decades before the [[Horus Heresy]], Fateweaver appeared before [[Lorgar Aurelian]] during his pilgrimage into the [[Eye of Terror]] and gave him a choice that would change the fate of galactic history. Using his foresight of the future he stated that Lorgar could either seek revenge against [[Roboute Guilliman]] for his shame upon [[Khur]], but doom Chaos in the [[Horus Heresy|coming war]], or put aside personal satisfaction and work for the [[Chaos Gods|Gods of Chaos]] and perhaps ensure their victory over the galaxy. In this single, important instance both of Fateweaver's heads spoke the same truth.{{Fn|6}} Later on during the actual Heresy Kairos fought [[Lion El'Jonson]], but was impaled through the heart as the Primarch remarked that he wondered if Fateweaver saw that coming.{{Fn|7}}

At some point after the fall of [[Prospero]], he was found by the Thousand Sons bound in a device known as the '''Iron Oculus'''. [[Magnus the Red]] ordered the Oculus to be brought into his possession, and [[Ahzek Ahriman]] was successful in retrieving it from the [[Yokai]]. Fateweaver was then brought from the Oculus into a [[Yokai]] under the name '''Aforgomon''', whereupon he aided Ahriman in recovering the [[Shards of Magnus]]. During his time with Ahriman's Cabal, Aforgomon was able to manipulate [[Hathor Maat]], desperate for salvation from the [[flesh change]], into changing a single line of the [[Book of Magnus]].{{Fn|10}}

On [[Nikaea]], Aforgomon was finally able to manifest into his proper form through Hathor Maat due to a pact made with Ahriman. After manifesting, he aided Ahriman in confronting the shard of Magnus, and the primarch revealed that the [[daemon]] was known as "The One Who Comes at the Appointed Time" before trapping the daemon with warp power. When Ahriman found Magnus to be too powerful, the sorcerer demanded more power, which the daemon gave, and he was able to merge with a portion of Magnus to battle the other before he released the daemon. After the shards of Magnus merged, Magnus transported the Thousand Sons back to the [[Planet of Sorcerers]] and the daemon vanished.{{Fn|10}}

====Recent History====
*913.[[M41]] The [[Purging of Jollana]] - Fateweaver injures Brother-Captain [[Caddon Varn]] of the [[Grey Knights]] before being decapitated by a [[Nemesis Dreadknight]].{{fn|5}}
*998.M41 - A Greater [[Daemon]] tentatively identified by the [[Imperium]] as Fateweaver was banished back to the [[Warp]] by the [[White Consuls]] during an engagement near the [[Eye of Terror]].{{Fn|2}}
*~999.M41 - Fateweaver is summoned by [[Abaddon]] to prevent the reborn [[Roboute Guilliman]] from reaching [[Terra]]. In the [[Terran Crusade]] Fateweaver and his [[Red Corsairs]] allies succeed in capturing Guilliman and his followers, but they are freed by [[Cypher]] and [[Sylandri Veilwalker]].{{Fn|9}}

'''Kaitheron''' was a [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] in the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], during the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
{{Spoiler|source=Galaxy in Flames (Novel)}}
When [[Isstvan III]]'s [[Planetary Governor]], [[Vardus Praal]], rebelled against the [[Imperium]], Kaitheron was among the [[Emperor's Children]] that helped to end the revolt. His squadron was among the first wave chosen by their [[Primarch]], [[Fulgrim]], to land upon the world and the [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] later aided [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]]{{Fn|1a}} in attacking Praal's bodyguard, which allowed Lucius to kill the corrupted Governor{{Fn|1b}}. Soon after Praal's death, however, [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]] revealed his [[Horus Heresy|treachery]] and unleashed several [[Virus Bomb]]s onto Isstvan III. This began the [[Sons of Horus]], [[Emperor's Children]], [[Death Guard]] and [[World Eaters]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legions]]' [[Battle of Isstvan III|purging]] of the Legionaries their [[Traitor|traitorous]] Primarchs, had deemed to be too [[Loyalist|loyal]] to the [[Emperor]].{{Fn|1c}}

Kaitheron and the few remaining members of his squadron, were able to survive both the [[Virus Bomb]]s and the firestorm that followed. Afterwards, they later regrouped with other surviving [[Loyalist]]s in [[Isstvan III]]'s '''Precentor's Palace'''. As a result, the Palace became a target for the [[Traitor]]s as they sought to kill any surviving Loyalists and Kaitheron defended it from countless attacks. He was later stationed by [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Saul Tarvitz]], to guard a section of the Palace protected by Loyalists led by Captain Lucius. Unfortunately for the [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]], Lucius would later seek to save himself and made contact with his [[Traitor Legions|traitorous Legion]]{{Fn|1d}}. After being told he could rejoin the [[Emperor's Children]] if he aided the Traitors, Lucius killed Kaitheron and the other Loyalists that served under him. With their deaths, the section they guarded was left unprotected and the Traitors were able to enter the Palace. Led by [[Lord Commander]] [[Eidolon]], they then launched an attack on the unsuspecting Loyalist survivors - which ensured that Lucius was able to rejoin his [[Primarch]] and his Legion.{{Fn|1e}}

'''Kal Jerico''' (in some sources - '''Jericho'''){{Fn|3}} is the most famous [[bounty hunter]] in [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]]'s [[Hive Primus]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
{{Spoiler|source=Kal Jerico (Graphic Novel Series)}}
Born the son of Necromunda's [[Planetary Governor]] [[Gerontius Helmawr]] and [[Inquisitor]] [[Heleana Jerico]] (which she later described as "just one of the many disagreeable things one has to do for the greater good of the Imperium"{{Fn|1}}), Kal left the luxury of the spire for the life of a bounty hunter in the [[Underhive]].{{Fn|1}}

As well as hunting those with bounties on their heads, Jerico often has a bounty on his own due to his unorthodox methods, leading as often as not to trouble finding him.  He resolves these situations using his trademark debonair swashbuckling style, relying on quick wits and his good luck more than brute strength.{{Fn|1}}

Most recently, Jerico has been summoned uphive a number of times to fulfil various missions for his family.{{Fn|3}}

===The Noble Spryer===
Kal Jericho and his partners, [[Yolanda Catallus]] and [[Scabbs]], were on a mission to capture a rogue ganger when they spot an agent of the crimelord [[Nemo]]. The bounty ended in an explosive mess, leading them to discover a new bounty: a [[vampire]] that has been killing and draining victims across the [[Underhive]]. They eventually discovered that the "vampire" in question was actually a blood-sucking [[Spyrer]]. Meanwhile, Kal was kidnapped and brought before [[Obidiah Clein]], who told him that the Spyrer was his half-brother [[Armand]] and that a noble family hunting team was sent to kill him.{{Fn|10a}}

Kal, alongside Obidiah's aid [[Valtin]], descended into the Hive City when the group discovered the noble hunting team in combat with [[House Escher]] gangers.{{Fn|10b}} As Yolanda and Scabbs were hunted by the Escher gangers, Kal and Valtin got word that Armand was nearby, and they descended on the area alongside the Escher Wildcats. After a chaotic free-for-all, Kal's team and the Wildcats agreed to an alliance to take down Armand.{{Fn|10c}} This combined force engaged Armand, but the Spyrer managed toe scape while kidnapping Valtin. It is eventually revealed that Armand contains a data cartridge which has the brain and memories of the last royal chamberlain, making him an object of interest for Obidiah Clein.{{Fn|10d}}

Valtin learned from her captor, Armand, that he intended to use the stolen brain to expose the corruption of [[House Helmawr]], allowing for a "cleansing" of the family. Kal and his allies then arrived and confronted Armand and tried to reason with him, but the Spryer refused to listen. In the final battle Armand was killed and Valtin was gravely wounded as the brain was taking by an agent working for Nemo.{{Fn|10e}} With Armand dead, Kal and his group escaped from the Escher gangers and noble mercenaries, intercepting Nemo's agent and acquiring his stolen data. Kal however decided that giving the cartridge to his father would be a mistake and gives it to a healed Valtin. Valtin was able to use the brain to outmaneuver their rivals and secure their place as heir apparent and a House reformer.{{Fn|10f}}

===Cardinal Crimson===
As Kal, Yolanda, and Scabbs take up a new bounty to pay off their gambling debt. The target is the powerful ganger [[Jobe Francks]], who was being hunted by [[Cardinal Crimson]], a powerful [[Redemptionist]] leader. As Francks avoided assassins with the help of a [[House Cawdor]] gang, Kal Jerico was confronted by [[Nemo]] and was forced to work for him to get his [[Cyber-Mastiff]], [[Wotan]], back.{{Fn|11a}} Kal, Yolanda, and Scabbs then came under attack from a group of debt-seeking Goliath gangers, but were aided by their Wildcat [[House Escher]] allies as well as Francks, who demonstrated his [[psychic]] abilities.{{Fn|11b}}

As Francks sought to learn why he is being hunted, Kal was able to track him down as Goliath and Cardinal Crimsons Redemptionists close in at a slave camp. Scabbs, having since been kidnapped and put to work in the camp, then led a slave revolt as chaos breaks out amidst the bounty hunters. The violence is all centered around a single glowing corpse. As Francks fled the assassins, Kal was captured by the Cardinal Crimson's men and tortured. The Cardinal offered Kal a deal: kill Francks and he would clear his debt. Kal was able to escape without overtly accepting the deal,{{Fn|11c}} and the "miracle body" at the center of the affair and slave revolt was revealed to be [[Syris Bowdie]], Francks psychic gang leader. Kal was then guided by Franck's powers, arriving and helping the slaves against the Cardinal Crimson's Redemptionists.{{Fn|11d}}

Kal then learned that Francks gang was a threat to the Cardinal Crimson slave operation, and confronted the Redemptionist leader. During their battle, both realize they were being manipulated by [[Nemo]]. In a fit of rage, the Cardinal was able to throw Francks off a cliff. In a final confrontation Kal, now with Francks psychic memories, caused the dome to collapse on the chaotic battle below. Kal was able to use Franck's final gift to find Wotan..{{Fn|11e}}

===Royal Wedding===
Still recovering from the Cardinal Crimson affair, Kal received a message delivering shocking news: that he is to be married to his partner [[Yolanda Catallus]], who is a duchess of [[House Catallus]]. Dragged off by House Helmawr Royal Guards{{Fn|12a}}, he learned that his father the [[Lord Helmawr]] is comatose and barely clinging to life from a prior assassination attempt. There was a package of advanced medicine to save him, but was stolen by the mysterious crimeboss [[Vandal Feg]]. Kal was able to get away and decided to find the package himself and learned that Vandal Feg was working with [[Nemo]], who was also pursuing the package.{{Fn|12b}}

Kal confronts his old colleague [[Valtin Schemko]], who revealed that Kal's wedding to Yolanda is in three days and he must find the package by then to avoid a civil war within the House. An assassin, [[Markel Bobo]], was also hired by another House guard [[Hermond Kauderer]] to kill Kal and expose the greater conspiracy. Kal and Scabbs decided to find Nemo, believing he had the package.{{Fn|12c}} The duo then allied with Captain [[Katerin]] of the Helmawr Royal Guard and were able to track down Nemo's lair and Vandal Feg. Battling through the guards, Kal outwitted Katerin and found Feg first, offering him help to escape if he helped him retrieve the package. Feg accepted but quickly escaped and revealed he had had the package all along.{{Fn|12d}} Feg, fleeing with the package, was nonetheless captured by Kal and Scabbs, who knew he would double-cross them. They recovered the package, but were confronted by Nemo and his men and would have been killed had it not been for the intervention of [[Wotan]], Kal's [[Cyber-Mastiff]].{{Fn|12e}}

Having retrieved the medicine for his father's recovery, Kal and Yolanda's forced wedding nonetheless carried on as planned. However the ceremony was interrupted by his cousin, Ramone, who revealed himself being behind the conspiracy. However the wedding had itself been a ruse by the Helmawr Household guard in order to draw out the true conspirators, and Lord Helmawr was revealed to be cured and awake. Chaos erupted across the ceremonial hall and Bobo reappeared to kill Ramone with a poison dart. As the violent dies down, Kal and Yolanda realize that they are, in fact, married.{{Fn|12e}}

===Sinner's Bounty===
As Kal, his "wife" Yolanda, and Scabbs discuss recent troubles, they were attacked by an enormous [[Mutant]] [[Slabscale]]. With the help of Wotan the group are able to kill Slabscale and flee, taking refuge in a watering settlement named [[Pipefall]]. They then discuss their intent to recover from their recent misfortunes by finding the dangerous [[Redemptionist]] [[Desolation Zoon]], who had a huge bounty on his head.{{Fn|13a}} Traveling through the Pipefall, Scabbs was angered by the treatment of Mutants and [[Abhuman]]s by local [[House Cawdor]] guards. This led to Scabbs freeing a fellow [[Ratskin]] woman named [[Amanute]], which caused Kal's team to become embroiled in a brawl between Cawdor and Mutant and [[Beastmen]] gangers under [[Gor Half-Horn]].{{Fn|13b}}

Allying with Half-Horn against House Cawdor, the group managed to escape on a ferry and learned the Beastmen bounty hunter was also seeking Zoon. Meanwhile, the Pastor [[Goeth]] learned of what Kal's group had done in Pipefall and informed his spymaster [[Nemo]] about the situation. Nemo revealed that he had placed a tracking device in Wotan and knows all of Kal's movements.{{Fn|13c}} As they fight through sump-beasts on the ferry with fellow bounty hunters, the group was able to arrive in [[Down Town]] and learned that Zoon was at the southern gate.{{Fn|13d}} Traveling to the southern gate and pursuing Zoon, the group fought off rival bounty hunter bikers and learned the Redemptionist was organizing local militia against a massing mutant attack under [[Queen Wart]].{{Fn|13e}} 

With the help of Amanute, who can control the horrifying beasts of the tunnels of Perdition, the group was able to move through the mutant lair in their pursuit of Zoon.{{Fn|13f}} The group was eventually infiltrated Perdition and were ambushed by Zoon's men, but Kal was able to negotiate a temporary alliance to fight off the mutants.{{Fn|13g}} The bounty hunters and Redemptionists defend Perdition against the Mutant hordes of Queen Wart, and Zoon is slain when his hauler exploded.{{Fn|13h}} The defenders are only saved thanks to Scabb and Amanute, who managed to rally the local Ratskins against the rest of the mutants. In the aftermath, the Ratskins have earned a place in the town and were now free.{{Fn|13i}}

Meanwhile, Nemo's agent Belladonna revealed she was able to use the chaos to escape with a black cylinder containing a [[Caryatid]]. The spymaster revealed he was working for an [[Inquisitor]], [[Jena Orechiel]], who ordered that Nemo continue to monitor Kal.{{Fn|13j}}

==Equipment==
Ambidextrous, Jerico wields two laser-sighted dueling [[laspistol]]s as his trademark and carries a trusty sabre.  He also uses [[Photon grenade|photon flash flares]] and [[frag grenade]]s to escape from unpleasant situations.{{Fn|4}}

==Associates & Enemies==
His associates include his half-[[Ratskin]] sidekick [[Scabbs]]{{Fn|1i}} and more recently his half-sister [[Merelda]]'s [[Cyber-Mastiff]] [[Wotan (Cyber-Mastiff)|Wotan]]{{Fn|1i}} and former enemy and fellow uphiver turned bounty hunter [[Yolanda Catallus]].{{Fn|1g}} He has been a member of the bounty hunter gang [[Kal Jerico's Profiteers]]{{Fn|7}} and the outcast gang [[Kal’s Heroes]].{{Fn|8}} 

The more ambivalent spy-master [[Nemo]] has called in a favour for saving Jerico's life on one occasion, while also sanctioning his lieutenant (and Jerico's enemy) [[Cheka]] to kill him. The faceless Nemo is Kal's most frequent enemy.{{Fn|10a}} Other enemies include the insane [[Redemptionist]] [[Cardinal Crimson (Redemption Cult)|Cardinal Crimson]]{{Fn|11a}}, escaped [[Pit Slave]] [[Vandal Feg]],{{Fn|9}} and [[Chrono-gladiator]] [[Krieger Thrax]].

(as Supreme Grand Master) |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Grey Knights]] |Notes = }} '''Kaldor Draigo''' is the 48th{{Fn|3}} and current [[Grey Knights Supreme Grand Master|Supreme Grand Master]] of the [[Grey Knights]]. He wields the legendary [[Titansword]].{{Fn|4}} ===Biography=== As a simple [[Battle-Brother]] of the [[3rd Brotherhood (Grey Knights)|3rd Brotherhood]], Draigo banished the [[Daemon Prince]] [[M'kar the Reborn]] on [[Acralem]].{{Fn|2a}} In 901.[[M41]], during the [[Battle of Kornovin]], Draigo would become Supreme Grand Master of the Grey Knights after the [[Daemon Prince]] [[Mortarion]] killed his predecessor, [[Geronitan]] along with many other Grey Knights who attempted to banish the fallen hero. The act made Draigo fly into a rage, assaulting the weakened Daemon Primarch. He was only able to defeat Mortarion by uttering the [[true name]] the Emperor had originally intended for him. The Primarch's body was shattered by this and Draigo carved his predecessor's name into his heart - an insult Mortarion never forgot, as his spirit recuperated in the [[Immaterium]] where he would prepare to kill Draigo once and for all.{{Fn|2b}}{{Fn|3}} ====Pandorax Campaign==== *{{Main|Pandorax Campaign}} {{Spoiler|source=Pandorax (Novel)}}'' [[Image:Draigo.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kaldor Draigo battles [[M'Kachen]]{{Fn|2c}}]] In 960.[[M41]] Draigo visited the body of the recently deceased [[Lexek Hasimir]]. Just as he was about to leave, it sat up and told him that the [[Damnation Cache]] was open and he must lead the chapter to [[Pythos]] to seal it.{{Fn|9a}} Draigo didn't have time to wait for Grey Knight reinforcements so he enacted an oath sworn to the Grey Knights by the [[Dark Angels]] calling them to aid him. [[Azrael]] initially refused, considering it blackmail. Draigo then revealed something he had learned while interrogating a [[Heretic Astartes]] prisoner, and Azrael committed the entire Dark Angels chapter to Pandorax - the sole concession Draigo gave was that the Dark Angels would have operational superiority.{{Fn|9b}} Once they arrived in [[Pandorax System|the system]], Draigo led the [[5th Brotherhood (Grey Knights)|5th Brotherhood]] on the ship ''[[Revenge]]'' into battle against [[Daemon]]s and [[Chaos Space Marine]]s. They were then reinforced by the Dark Angels, who had finished clearing an [[asteroid]] in the system. [[Gabriel]] met with Draigo, with Draigo's Knights and Gabriel's [[Deathwing]] fighting towards the portal they were trying to close. Once near the portal, Draigo and others started a ritual to seal it; however, at the start of the second phase he was interrupted by [[‘J’ian-Lo]], a [[Daemon Prince]] of [[Nurgle]]. The Prince grabbed Draigo and [[teleport]]ed them into space so he would be unable to hear Draigo use its [[true name]]. After a brief battle, Draigo was able to kill the Daemon, severing its head from its body and then throwing it into space. He was then teleported back into the ship and talked with [[Azrael]], [[Ezekiel]], and [[Gabriel]].{{Fn|9b}} ====Return to Acralem==== In 999.[[M41]], Draigo returned alone to [[Acralem]] to free it from [[M'kar]], hoping to end the Chapter's ancient feud with the Daemon.{{Fn|4}} However, after the fight{{Fn|2a}} Draigo has been cursed to a life trapped within the [[Warp]], doomed to walk within the Realm of [[Chaos]] itself. To remain pure while constantly assailed by Chaos shows fortitude and personal strength that is beyond measure. He has undertaken many great exploits within the Warp: slaying the great [[Bloodthirster]] [[Kar'Voth]], setting fire to the jungles of [[Nurgle]]'s domain, defeating the six chosen [[Daemonettes]] of [[Slaanesh]], the [[Six Sisters]], and destroying the fortress of the [[Lord of Change]] [[M'Kachan]].{{Fn|2c}} While Draigo lives, he will prevail and one day, he will return.{{Fn|1}} ====Age of the Dark Imperium==== After the formation of the [[Great Rift]], Draigo discovered that he could now return to the material realm for greater periods of time. The Grey Knights [[Prognosticar]]s believe that his presence is now linked to Mortarion due to the ties of hatred that bind the two. Draigo later appeared to each of the Grand Masters of the Chapter and asked for their counsel, and due to the dire state of the Imperium the [[Terminus Decree]] is given consideration.{{Fn|5}} During the [[Assault on Sortiarius]], Draigo reappeared to help guide the Imperial forces.{{Fn|6}} Despite this, the Grey Knights have decided that if Draigo can not escape his curse soon than a new Supreme Grand Master will have to be named.{{Fn|8}} ===Images=== Image:KaldorDraigo01.jpg|Miniature Image:JoytoyGreKaldor.jpg|Joytoy Draigo figure{{Fn|7}} ===See also=== *[[List of Chapter Masters]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: http://www.games-workshop.com/en-US/Grey-Knights-Lord-Kaldor-Draigo (last accessed 15 April 2015) *2: [[Codex: Grey Knights (5th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|2a}}: pgs. 14–17 **{{Endn|2b}}: pg. 38 **{{Endn|2c}}: pg. 39 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Mortarion's Heart]] *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Grey Knights (7th Edition)]] — ''Deeds of Legend'' *{{Endn|5}}: [[Codex: Grey Knights (8th Edition)]], pg. 25 *{{Endn|6}}: [[Psychic Awakening: Ritual of the Damned]], pgs. 16-17 *{{Endn|7}}: [https://www.joytoy.com/products/grey-knights-kaldor-draigo Joytoy Draigo figure] ''(last accessed 21 July 2024)'' *{{Endn|8}}: [[Codex: Grey Knights (10th Edition)]], pg. 15 *9: [[Pandorax (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|9a}}: Interlude **{{Endn|9b}}: Chapter 9 {{GKUnits}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Draigo, Kaldor}} [[Category:Characters (Grey Knights)]] [[de:Kaldor Draigo]] [[fr:Kaldor Draigo]]

Kaleb Arin.wikitext:
{{DeathGuardPortal}}
'''Kaleb Arin''' was the [[Equerry|Housecarl]] to [[Space Marine Captain|Battle-Captain]] [[Nathaniel Garro]] of the [[Death Guard]].

== Biography ==
{{spoiler|source=The Flight of the Eisenstein (Novel)}}
According to Captains [[Typhus|Typhon]] and [[Ignatius Grulgor|Grulgor]], Arin was one of many human [[Aspirant]]s to the [[Death Guard]], who failed miserably but could not bring himself to end his own life. These Captains, however, were known for their disdain of non-[[Astartes]] humans.

As Captain of the 7th Company, Garro was traditionally entitled to an [[equerry]], and chose Arin, whose duties included overseeing the maintenance and repair of Garro's [[Power Armour]] and his sword, ''[[Libertas]]''. Garro valued Arin's service, and relied on his discretion. In particular, he asked Arin to keep his ears open when Garro discovered the existence of secret lodges forming among the Death Guard's elite warriors.

Arin later met a heroic end aboard the frigate ''[[Eisenstein]]'' over [[Isstvan III]]. While [[Ignatius Grulgor]] prepared to bomb the surface of the world with [[Life Eater]] virus capsules, Garro tried to stop him. When Grulgor tried to shoot Garro, Kaleb fired at Grulgor's gun with his own, knocking it off target. Grulgor responded by stabbing Arin with a combat knife, but the stray bolter round hit one of the Life-Eater capsules, releasing the deadly virus.

Arin threw himself onto the emergency release switch, sealing himself, Grulgor and the other Traitor Astartes inside the launch bay, to protect Garro and his company. As he did so, he shouted to his Captain that Garro was "of purpose," and that he must survive, no matter what. After he died, Garro found the [[Lectitio Divinitatus]] in Arin's belongings, realizing that he was a secret follower of the [[Imperial Cult|cult]] of the deified [[Emperor]].

During the ''Eisenstein'''s voyage through the [[Warp]], Arin was revived as a grotesque revenant by [[Nurgle]]'s plague attack, but was quickly dispatched by Garro.

Kalimos.wikitext:
{{EmperorsChildrenPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion's]] [[17th Company (Emperor's Children)|17th Company]], during the [[Horus Heresy]] and like most of its members he had embraced mutilation, hedonism, and body-modification.{{Fn|1a}}

Shortly after the [[Dropsite Massacre]], Kalimos was among the Legion's [[Brotherhood of the Phoenix]], who came to a meeting called by Captain [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]] and were convinced by him that a [[Daemon]] has possessed their [[Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]].  Incensed at the idea{{Fn|1a}}, the Brotherhood devised a plan to ambush the Primarch aboard the [[Strike Cruiser]] ''[[Andronicus]]'', when Fulgrim was due to visit the lab of [[Chief Apothecary]] [[Fabius]]{{Fn|1b}}, and then find a way to force the Daemon to leave his body{{Fn|1a}}.  However, during the ambush, Fulgrim proved himself to be a deadly opponent, despite being vastly outnumbered and seriously wounded Kalimos.  Though the ambush was successful{{Fn|1c}}, Kalimos's body had to be biologically restored by Fabius and Fulgrim was tortured to free him of the Daemon's control.  However, the Primarch quickly revealed that his capture had been a ruse and easily freed himself{{Fn|1d}}.  The Primarch admitted that while his body had been controlled by a Daemon, which happened after Fulgrim's shock at killing his brother [[Ferrus Manus]], this had allowed him to come to a better understanding of the powers given to him by his worship of [[Slaanesh]].  This later allowed the Primarch to retake control of his body and Fulgrim stated that he was now ready to share the secrets he had learned with his Legion.{{Fn|1f}}

Later, Kalimos was part of the combined force of Emperor's Children and [[Iron Warriors]] that journeyed into the [[Eye of Terror]] in search of the [[Angel Exterminatus]].  While en route, they discovered the [[Iron Hands]] [[Strike Cruiser]] ''[[Sisypheum]]'', which had been damaged and vulnerable to attack.  The Emperor's Children aboard the ''[[Andronius]]'' attempted to board the vessel, while the Iron Hands attempted to repel them.{{Fn|2a}}  Eventually [[Iron Father|Frater]] [[Thamatica]] was able to restore the ship's motive systems, ramming and destroying the ''Andronius''.{{Fn|2b}}  As a result, Kalimos was cast into the vacuum of space.  Although he survived and was brought onto the ''[[Iron Blood]]'', he succumbed to his wounds and died.{{Fn|2c}}  

After his death, [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]] took his whip for his own use.{{Fn|2c}}

'''Kallista Eris''' was a historiographer{{Fn|1a}} assigned to the [[28th Expedition]], specifically the [[Thousand Sons]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], during the [[Great Crusade]].  Eris was highly regarded in her role as a [[remembrancer]].{{Fn|1b}}

Eris had a psychic ability that allowed her divine future events, but came with violent seizures.  She had foreseen the [[Battle of Prospero|Burning of Prospero]] by the [[Space Wolves]] and was able to warn her fellow remembrancers [[Camille Shivani]] and [[Lemuel Gaumon]].

===History===
Eris was assigned as a remembrancer to the Thousand Sons Legion.  She was held in high regard by several of the members of that Legion, including [[Ahzek Ahriman]].{{Fn|1b}}  Blessed, or perhaps cursed, with a gift of foresight, Kallista possessed the ability to sense upcoming events, particularly those of incredible danger.  Horrific migraines always accompanied these flashes that put her into a trance-like state wherein she would write down, often in the simplest sense and a handful of words, the event that would occur.{{Fn|1c}}

Eris was present with the Thousand Sons during their investigation of [[Aghoru]].  That was where she predicted the Space Wolves would invade [[Prospero]].{{Fn|1}}  No one understood its true meaning until shortly before the actual attack.

Eris suffered a major seizure while on Prospero, requiring treatment from the Thousand Sons.  On [[Magnus|Magnus's]] orders, Ahriman and [[Ankhu Anen]] exploited Eris's link to the [[warp]].  The Astartes reasoned that their medical technology had saved Eris's life in the first instance, now that the Imperium of Man was under the threat of civil war, they believed risking Eris's life to gather knowledge of the impending civil war was justified.  They removed Eris from the warp-nullifying machine she had been surviving on and she ultimately died an exceedingly gruesome death.{{Fn|1d}}

Eris is known to have become romantically involved with [[Sokhem Vithara]].  After her death, she appears to have communicated with him requesting her ashes be delivered to her fellow remembrancers as they were about to flee the planet prior to the arriving Space Wolves.{{Fn|1e}}

Her ashes were placed in an urn carried by [[Lemuel Gaumon]] while imprisoned at Kamiti Sona for five years following his fleeing from Prospero.  After being rescued/captured by Knight-Errant [[Dio Promus]], [[Yasu Nagasena]], and a team of Space Wolves, Gaumon was separated from the urn.{{Fn|2a}}  After the team confronted a [[Shard of Magnus]], it was revealed that one was hidden within the urn, and the two shards merged.{{Fn|2b}}

===Prophecy===
Her last prophecy was ''“It’s too late... the Wolf is at the door and it hungers for blood. Oh, Throne... no, the blood! The Ravens, I see them too. The lost sons and a Raven of blood. They cry out for salvation and knowledge, but it is denied! A brother betrayed, a brother murdered. The worst mistake for the noblest reason! It cannot happen, but it must!"''{{Fn|1d}}

===Trivia===
It is a popular speculation among Warhammer 40,000 fans that the [[Blood Ravens]] Chapter are descended from the Thousand Sons, and that the line about the ''Raven of blood'' implies that the speculation is accurate.

[[Inquisitor]] '''Kalypsia''' was in charge of the [[Deathwatch]] kill-team detailed to deal with the [[Tyranid]] outbreak on [[Herodian IV]].

==History==
{{spoiler|source=Warrior Brood (Novel)}}
The team's objective was to eliminate the [[Hive Tyrant]], but during the first drop, two members of her team were killed in a [[Lictor]] ambush and a third was killed by [[Zoanthrope]]s. Having escaped that fate, she interviewed an [[Adeptus Mechanicus]] survivor from the planet and supposedly killed him after discovering the existence of a secret weapon.

Her team was reinforced with [[Space Marines]] from the [[Mantis Warriors]] [[Chapter]], who had taken heavy losses from an earlier engagement with the Tyranids. With their help, she and the remaining members of her Deathwatch squad discovered and retrieved the weapon, which turned out to be a mix of [[Imperial]] and [[Eldar]] technology and Tyranid [[bio-morph]]s, fused to the body of [[Inquisitor]] [[Grendal]].

[[Librarian]] [[Shaiden]] and [[Chaplain]] [[Broec]] stayed behind to kill the Hive Tyrant, supposedly dying in the process. They succeeded and the swarm was confused long enough for the rest to be extracted from the surface. Kalypsia was knocked out when she examined the machine back in the [[Thunderhawk]]: it turned out Grendal was possessed by the machine. He tried to kill Kalypsia, but died instantly when he left the chair, since it was the only thing keeping him alive.

When no one was around, she attached herself to the machine, which had the same effect on her. The [[Captain]] of the team, [[Octavius]], opened the bay airlock and threw a plasma grenade onto the possessed Kalypsia's lap before was sucked out into space; she and the machine were destroyed in the plasma blast.

Kanath.wikitext:
{{CSMPortal}}
'''Kanath''' is a [[Chaos Lord|Agitor]] in the [[Sons of Malice]] [[Chaos Warband|Warband]] and commanded several warships during the [[13th Black Crusade]]{{Fn|1a}}, with the [[Strike Cruiser]] [[Bronze Minos]] serving as his flagship.

His fleet took part in the Chaos invasion of the [[Agripinaa System]]{{Fn|1b}} and after [[Cadia]]'s destruction{{Fn|1c}}, they fell upon the ships of [[General]] [[Gruber]]{{Fn|1a}}, which had escaped from the [[Cadian System]]{{Fn|1c}}. In doing so, Kanath sought to claim revenge for the Cadians' part in purging the Warband's Homeworld [[Scelus]], which he narrowly escaped from,{{Fn|1a}} and his fleet mercilessly destroyed many of the General's fleeing ships. This forced Gruber to quickly order his remaining ships to [[Morten's Quay]]'s ice mining moon, [[Faith's Anchorage]], where he deployed his surviving forces. The General then charged the [[Lord-Lieutenant Berwicke]] and the [[Venerable Warrior]] to flee and reach [[Terra]]{{Fn|1b}}, but both ships were destroyed before they could escape the System{{Fn|1d}}. Afterwards, Kanath's fleet returned to the moon and he ordered his forces to invade the moon and kill the Cadians. This began the [[Battle of Faith's Anchorage]]{{Fn|1e}} and the outnumbered Cadians were overwhelmed by the Sons of Malice and the hordes of slaves they had at their command. Before the Cadians were killed, several other Chaos Warbands arrived{{Fn|1f}} and helped massacre the few survivors that still remained{{Fn|1g}}. This was not the end of the battle, however, as the Chaos Warbands were unaware that another Imperial fleet fleeing from Cadia, had also arrived in the system. Led by [[Admiral]] [[d'Armitage]], the Imperial fleet launched a surprise attack on the Chaos warships in Faith's Anchorage's orbit while the majority of their forces were still on the moon. Caught between the need to either fight or gather their forces from the moon, only a few managed to escape from the battle{{Fn|1h}}. Afterwards, General [[Isaia Bendikt]] deployed his Cadians to Faith's Anchorage, and in two weeks they purged the forces of Chaos from the moon's surface. It is not known if Kanath was killed in the battle.{{Fn|1g}}

(as Phoenix Lord){{Fn|1}} |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Craftworld Eldar]] *[[Ynnari]] (former) |Notes }} '''Karandras''' (translation, ''"The Shadow Hunter"'') is the [[Eldar]] [[Phoenix Lord]] of the [[Striking Scorpions]] [[Aspect]]. === History === Karandras is the most shadowy and mysterious of the Phoenix Lords as no one knows where his shrine originally lay, though it is thought to be one of the smaller [[Craftworlds]] that survived [[The Fall]] but were destroyed soon after. Karandras is also not the first [[Exarch]] of the [[Striking Scorpions]], as that honour belongs to [[Arhra]], the Father of Scorpions. However, Arhra fell to darkness and betrayed the other Phoenix Lords, leading [[daemon]]s in an attack on the [[Asur|Shrine of Asur]]. Arhra would flee into the [[Webway]] becoming forever known as ''"the Fallen Phoenix that burns with the light of [[Chaos]]."'' Karandras, the greatest pupil of [[Arhra]], took his master's place after a brutal seventeen day duel with him and tempered his murderous nature with the patience of a hunter, using his new teachings to found Aspect Shrines on many Craftworlds.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}}{{Fn|3}}{{Fn|4a}} Karandras is the ultimate stealth warrior, able to draw the very shadows around himself and kill his prey with claw and blade before they were ever aware of his presence. He carries the [[Scorpion's Claw]] ''[[Arhra's Bane]]'', the [[Biting Blade]] ''[[Isirmathil]]'', and [[Plasma Grenades]]. Perhaps his most potent weapon is his [[Mandiblaster]] known as the [[Scorpion's Bite]].{{Fn|3}} The Mandiblasters of other Scorpions are as pinpricks compared to the Scorpion's Bite,{{Fn|1}} which is so powerful it can shatter the [[Power Armour]] of a [[Space Marine]] and hurl him off his feet{{Fn|4b}} or penetrate [[Terminator Armour]]{{Fn|6}} As with the other Phoenix Lords, Karandras has no permanent home and wanders across the galaxy. He was last spotted on [[Zandros]] in 928.[[M41]] where he dueled for seventeen days with Arhra.{{Fn|5}} Karandras later appeared under the command of [[Jain Zar]], now pledged to [[Ynnead]]. Karandras took part in the battle to defend the [[Ynnari]] against the [[Thousand Sons]] and [[Tzeentch]] [[Daemon]]s in the [[Webway]], vanishing during the struggle.{{Fn|8}} ===Images=== Karandras.jpg|Miniature{{Fn|7}} Karandras 2.jpg|Karandras fighting a Space Marine of the [[Black Templars]] Chapter Karandras by Sam Wood.jpeg|Karandras The Shadow Hunter ===See Also=== *[[Shadow Sect of Karandras]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Eldar (2nd Edition)]], Pg. 84 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Codex: Eldar (3rd Edition)]], Pg. 42 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Eldar (4th Edition)]], Pg. 56 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Path of the Warrior (Novel)]] by [[Gav Thorpe]] **{{Endn|4a}}: Anger, Pg. 130 **{{Endn|4b}}: Death, Pg. 402 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Warhammer 40,000 5th Edition Rulebook]], Pg. 128 *{{Endn|6}}: [[Codex: Craftworlds (7th Edition)]], (e-book) ''Karandras - Remnants of Glory'' *{{Endn|7}}: http://www.games-workshop.com/en-US/Phoenix-Lord-Karandras ''(last accessed 7 May 2015)'' *{{Endn|8}}: [[Gathering Storm: Fracture of Biel-Tan]] {{EldarUnits}} [[Category:Characters (Craftworld Eldar)]] [[Category:Phoenix Lords]] [[de:Karandras]]

Karedo.wikitext:
{{AdeptusCustodesPortal}}
'''Karedo''' was a [[Tharanatoi]] in the [[Legio Custodes]]' [[Hetaeron Companions]], who took part in the [[Horus Heresy]]'s [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
A proven exemplar of the [[Legio Custodes|Custodes]]' excellence,{{Fn|2}} he was among the one hundred [[Hetaeron Companions]]{{Fn|1e}} that [[Caecaltus Dusk]] commanded as the [[Emperor]] led a [[Teleportation]] attack on [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]]' flagship, the [[Vengeful Spirit]]. But due to Horus' machinations, the strike force's teleportation separated them all and the Emperor and the Companions found themselves alone within one of the Spirit's hanger bays.{{Fn|1b}} Soon afterwards, though, the Warmaster is able to manipulate the Companions' minds and convinces them that the Emperor must die. With this overwhelming thought, the Companions attack the Emperor and He is forced to kill many of them, before He can gather enough of His [[psychic]] might to clear the Custodes' minds of Horus' influence.{{Fn|1c}} The Companions have been ravaged, however, and few are still alive to protect the Emperor, as He ventures further into the Vengeful Spirit.{{Fn|1d}}

Their respite is short lived though, as the [[Chaos Gods]] strike and cloud the [[Hetaeron Companions|Companions]]' minds to the environment around them. This allows the [[Daemons]] infesting the [[warp]]-tainted [[Vengeful Spirit]] to silently attack the [[Legio Custodes|Custodes]] and many are killed this way, before the [[Emperor]] notices what is happening. Once more He is forced to use his [[psychic]] powers to clear the Companions' minds, but at this point only Karedo, [[Caecaltus Dusk]], [[Xadophus]], [[Taurid]], [[Ravengast]], [[Nmembo]] and [[Zagrus]] still live.{{Fn|1e}} As they venture further into the Vengueful Spirit they begin to be attacked on all sides and the Emperor extends his psychic might into the surviving Companions. Though their minds are still their own, the Custodes' become an extension of the Emperor's will and their eight bodies are controlled by His mind, as He searches for [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]].{{Fn|2}}

'''Kargos''', known as '''The Bloodspitter''', was an [[Apothecary]] in the [[8th Company (World Eaters)|8th Company]] of the [[World Eaters]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}}

===Biography===
A member of [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Khârn]]'s [[Space Marine Command Squad|command squad]], he earned his nickname "Bloodspitter" for his habit of spitting blood into the eyes of his enemies in arena combat aboard the [[Conqueror (Ship)|Conqueror]].{{Fn|1e}} During these bouts Kargos was often paired with the ferocious [[Blood Angels]] Captain [[Nassir Amit]].{{Fn|1d}} The two gained a strong bond, particularly after [[Sanguinius]] and [[Angron]] themselves witnessed a much-publicized fight to the death with two World Eaters champions.{{Fn|3b}} Uncharacteristically for the World Eaters [[Legion]], Kargos possessed a great sense of humor and wit and often used it to calm his comrades during their rages.{{Fn|1c}}

Kargos followed his legion into rebellion, and helped to kill his loyalist brethren during the [[Battle of Isstvan III]]. In the battle's aftermath, he saved the life of Khârn who had been horribly wounded in combat.{{Fn|1b}} By the [[Siege of Terra]], Kargos had succumbed fully to madness, his Apothecary tools broken. He nonetheless was the one to discover the body of Khârn after his battle with [[Sigismund]], taking up his former Captain's [[Chain Axe]] ''[[Gorechild]]''.{{Fn|3c}} Guided by the [[Word Bearers]] [[Chaplain]] [[Inzar Taerus]], Kargos took part in the invasion of the [[Inner Palace]]. During an assault on a refugee convoy, Kargos was met by his former chain-brother Nassir Amit and had his throat cut. However he was able to recover, swearing retribution against Amit who simply told him to "eat shit [sic], traitor".{{Fn|3a}}

Next, Kargos was part of the horde that assailed the [[Eternity Gate (Imperial)|Eternity Gate]]. During the battle he nearly slew [[Arkhan Land]], killing his pet cyber-monkey [[Sapien]]. Later in the vicious melee he again came to blows with Nassir Amit. Kargos was again defeated, and as he lay dying on the ground was mocked for his weakness by Chaplain Taerus.{{Fn|3b}}

Despite his mortal wounds, he somehow recovered and even managed to escape [[Terra]] after [[Horus]]'s death. He joined the bulk of the now-leaderless World Eaters fleet during the [[Great Scouring]], and killed the captain of one company to take charge of his warriors. Thus, Kargos rose to lead his own [[Chaos Warband|warband]], and even served in the Legion's consultative "Enclave".{{Fn|5}} At some point, he also became a [[Chaos Champion]] of [[Khorne]].{{Fn|2}} When the World Eaters ultimately sought refuge at [[Skalathrax]] in the [[Eye of Terror]], finding the world already claimed by the [[Emperor's Children]], Kargos was one of the commanders advocating for an immediate attack.{{Fn|5}}

'''Karl''' is a [[Wolf Priest]] in the [[Space Wolves]] [[Chapter]]{{Fn|1a}}, where he serves as both a mentor and potent healer{{Fn|1b}}. During his service to the Space Wolves, he joined a strike force commanded by the [[Grey Hunter]] [[Valgard Twice-Slain]]{{Fn|1a}}, whose induction into the Chapter Karl had personally overseen{{Fn|1b}}, and was besides the Grey Hunter when disaster struck their [[Strike Cruiser]] as they emerged from the [[Warp]] near the [[Imperium]] world [[Kanak]]. Without warning, they were ambushed by a [[Word Bearers]] [[Murder Class Cruiser]] and their Strike Cruiser crashed in pieces onto Kanak{{Fn|1c}}. Karl was among those who survived and discovered that Kanak had been successfully invaded by a Word Bearers Warband led by the [[Dark Apostle]] [[Oriax (Word Bearers)|Oriax the Persuader]], whose forces began mercilessly hunting the Space Wolves down. In the ensuing battles that followed, Valgard quickly organized Karl and the other survivors of the strike force he found and began taking the fight to the Word Bearers. As the group now fights across the fallen Imperium world, Karl serves as a trusted adviser to Valgard and fights ferociously against any traitors the Space Wolves come across.{{Fn|1a}}

Kasdar.wikitext:
{{IronHandsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a member of the [[Iron Hands]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] during the [[Horus Heresy]], and was a survivor of the [[Dropsite Massacre]]. Two years after that horrific event, Kasdar was one of the [[Legio Astartes|Legionaries]] of the [[Shattered Legions]], who answered the [[Primarch]] [[Corax]]'s rallying call on [[Scarato]]. Once there he listened to the Primarch, as he asked those of the Shattered Legions, as well as [[Loyalist]]s of the [[Traitor Legions]], to join forces with his [[Raven Guard]]; in order to strike back at those who had betrayed the [[Imperium]]. After hearing this, some of those present were left unconvinced that their few numbers could do anything of worth, but Corax answered that his tactics would help them win wars against their far superior foe. To prove this, he asked those present to aid his Legion, in liberating the Imperium world [[Carandiru]] from [[Horus]]' control and witness first hand how powerful their combined forces were. Afterwards the Primarch said, if they still did not agree to continue to fight beside the Raven Guard, they would be free to go. All those present agreed to this{{Fn|1a}} and Carandiru was successfully liberated. Whether Kasdar continued to aid the Raven Guard afterwards though, is unknown.{{Fn|1b}}

Kasimir De Valtos.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Kasimir de Valtos''' was the head of the de Valtos industrial cartel on the world of [[Pavonis]]{{Fn|1}}.

==History==
During one of his trips off-planet, his ship was ambushed by [[Dark Eldar]] pirates and de Valtos was tortured almost to death.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}

The experience left his body shattered, wracked with constant physical pain and his senses dulled so that he was unable to taste food or drink{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}.{{Fn|1c}} It also drove him insane, though this was not apparent to his allies or enemies.

Outwardly, he withdrew from the active management of his cartel, and invested large sums in archaeological expeditions across the planet. To the rest of Pavonis, he was admired as a patron of the arts and a connoisseur of antiquities, as well as pitied for surviving his ordeal.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}

Inwardly, he was obsessed with repairing his broken body and inflicting revenge on the whole galaxy for his suffering. In the short term, he kidnapped men and women and personally tortured them to death, while also undergoing surgeries from the Dark Eldar, with whom he had allied himself (paradoxically, by undergoing torture at the Dark Eldar's hands he gained [[Kyerzak|a measure of respect and authority]] among them).{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1d}} In the long term, he used his wealth to fund an obsessive search for the [[Nightbringer]], an ancient [[C'tan]] deity that ancient scrolls had said was located on Pavonis. de Valtos believed that releasing the entity from its prison would allow him to become immortal and nearly omnipotent.{{Fn|1e}}

Allying himself with [[Vendare Taloun]], he staged a coup d'etat on Pavonis, ousting Governor [[Mykola Shonai]] by military force, and taking her and [[Inquisition|Inquisitor]] [[Ario Barzano]] prisoner. Both were freed from de Valtos's estate by Captain [[Uriel Ventris]], but not before de Valtos and his Dark Eldar allies had unearthed the Nightbringer.

It was only after they had released it, that he comprehended the sheer age and destructive power of the Nightbringer, and realized that it had no need to notice him, much less reward him in any way. He was reduced to begging for immortality, before the Nightbringer casually struck off his head.{{Fn|1f}}

In the aftermath of his death, the de Valtos cartel disintegrated, and his estate on Pavonis was abandoned. Several other cartels fell into disarray, their leaders having been killed by de Valtos shortly before the coup began. Taloun was convicted of treason and executed.

Kasmoteph.wikitext:
{{NecronsPortal}}
'''Kasmoteph the Silent''' is a [[Necron]] [[Cryptek|Chronomancer]] of the [[Nekthyst Dynasty]].{{Fn|2a}}

==History==
Kasmoteph used scanners he designed himself to discover the trace of a powerful relic{{Fn|2b}} aboard the ''[[Savant (Ship)|Savant]]'', an [[Adeptus Mechanicus]] vessel.{{Fn|1a}} Not wanting his lord [[Nekhtoshar the Immeasurable]] to take credit for securing the prize, Kasmoteph prepared a retinue consisting of [[Immortal]]s, [[Canoptek Wraith]]s, [[Deathmark]]s and [[Necron Warrior|Warriors]], and proceeded to raid the vessel without his lord's consent.{{Fn|2a}}

He used chronomancy to cripple the ship without harming the precious contents within{{Fn|2b}}, allowing his forces to board and easily deal with the resistance.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|2d}}{{Fn|3a}} Initially, Kasmoteph gloated as his plan unfolded successfully{{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|2c}}, but he would later realize he underestimated the relic's power.{{Fn|2d}} When [[Magos|Magos Technicus]] [[Tathyk Shon]] sought to activate it,{{Fn|3b}}{{Fn|3c}} Kasmoteph unleashed his chrono-immaterial powers.{{Fn|3c}}{{Fn|3d}} His attempt was disrupted by a malevolent sentience, and locked the entire raid in a temporal loop.{{Fn|3d}}

Kasmoteph the Silent wields an [[aeonstave]], a powerful weapon used to manipulate time itself.{{Fn|3b}}

'''Kasper Ansbach Hawser''', also known as '''Ahmad Ibn Rustah''', was a human academic of some significance to the [[Imperium of Man]] prior to the [[Horus Heresy]]. Hawser was noted to disappear under mysterious circumstances at about the age of 80 only to reappear years later as a skjald, or oral historian, for the [[Space Wolves]] around the outset of the Horus Heresy.  

=== Background ===
====Early History====
He was born approximately 862.[[M30]]. The earliest records pertaining to Hawser, at 3 or 4 years old, note that he was discovered by a surveying patrol in the radland flats near the outskirts of the great city of Ur, on Terra. His parents were believed to have been killed in an attack by a group of predators, likely wolves. Hawser was apparently spared the same fate by mere chance. He was brought to Ur's Catheric commune and raised by a Rector named Uwe. Hawser was given an education and was noted to have been a bright child. {{Fn|1a}}. Uwe named him Kasper Hawser after the folktale of [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caspar_Hauser Casper Hauser], noting the similarities of circumstances in which Hawser was discovered. {{Fn|1b}}

====Career====
After graduating from the Univesitariate of Sardis with honours {{Fn|1d}}, Hawser completed his education and earned a doctorate degree. While it is never specifically mentioned, it was likely in archaeology or a similar discipline.{{Fn|1c}} He is noted to have founded the [[Conservatory Project]] and served as its director. He was awarded the [[Prix Daumarl]], for steadfast contributions towards the definition and accomplishment of Terran Unification in 902.M30.{{Fn|1c}} He was acclaimed by academicians throughout the Imperium. He authored several research papers noted to have inspired new areas of research and development resulting in profound improvements for society.{{Fn|1b}}

Concerned that the Conservatory Project would be annexed by the [[Administratum]], Hawser took a sabbatical. He proposed he would do field work for approximately a year. It was at this point that Hawser mysteriously disappeared from Imperium records and it was likely then that he was unknowingly compromised by [[Chaos]] and turned into a sleeper agent.{{Fn|1b}}

====Space Wolves====
Hawser travelled to [[Fenris]] under the name Ahmad Ibn Rustah. He made numerous requests to land and was eventually given permission and specific coordinates by the Space Wolves. In error, Hawser's ship was shot down by [[Bjorn the Fell-Handed]]. He crashed on the surface and was found by the indigenous people of Fenris and kept safe until he was ultimately rescued by Bjorn. Suffering significant injuries from the crash, Hawser was given medical treatment by the Wolves and augmented as well. His physical strength and speed were enhanced, as well as the vision in his right eye. He was kept in stasis by the Wolves for 19 Fenrisian years (57-76 [[Terra]]n years{{fn|1a}}) after discovering he was a spy.

Awoken, Hawser, now a skjald of Tra (3rd Company) pursued his research into the Space Wolves Legion, while the Wolves observed his behaviour and further determined his motives as a spy. Hawser was present with the Wolves during their operations as part of the [[40th Expeditionary Fleet]]{{Fn|1e}}, the [[Council of Nikaea]]{{Fn|1b}}, and the [[Burning of Prospero]]{{Fn|1e}}.

It was at the [[Council of Nikaea]] that Hawser met privately with [[Leman Russ (Primarch)|Leman Russ]]. It was then he was informed by Russ of his status as a spy for the Thousand Sons. Hawser, of course, was shocked by these accusations and fully cooperated with the Wolves. It was suspected by all that the Thousand Sons had used sorcery to possess Hawser unconsciously and pass information onto that legion.{{Fn|1b}}

====Chaos====
Hawser continued to have a recurring dream recalling his time staying in a luxury suite on the Lemuryan plate, above Terra. After leaving the Conservatory Project, Hawser had taken up residence on the plate to become acclimatized to his impending space travel. During the dream, Hawser would go through a routine of waking to an alarm and getting ready for the day. As he caught his reflection in a mirror, he would note that there was another reflection of someone behind him. At this point he would continue to wake up and was unable to recall who was standing behind him.{{Fn|1e}}

As Hawser worked with the Wolves to discover his true mission to Fenris, this dream became a focal point of their investigations. Ultimately it was discovered that the dream was actually a suppressed memory of his contact with an unknown agent of chaos (daemon). It was speculated by the Wolves that Hawser may have been developed as a future agent for over 50 years—if not his entire life.{{Fn|1b}} It is understood that the contact on the Lemuryan plate appears to be the point he ceased being Hawser and became Ahmad Ibn Rustah and essentially turning him into an active, if unwitting, pawn for Chaos.

Hawser later encountered the daemon two more times. The first was during the Council of Nikaea, where the daemon masqueraded as Captain [[Amon]] of the Thousand Sons. The purpose of this contact was to further the illusion that Hawser was in fact a [[Hidden One]]. The second encounter occurred during the Burning of Prospero. While participating in Space Wolves' assault of the planet, Hawser encountered the daemon who this time masqueraded as [[Horus]]. The daemon informed Hawser of its plan for him, suggesting that all along the goal had been to turn two loyal legions against each other in the hopes of their mutual annihilation. The reason was that the Wolves were the only real threat to the [[Luna Wolves]] legion, and the Thousand Sons' psyker abilities posed a great danger to Chaos' overall strategy. By negating these two threats in one stroke, Chaos' ability to destroy the Imperium of Man was assured. {{Fn|1e}}

The daemon that had infiltrated Hawser was subsequently defeated by the Space Wolves and its plan revealed. Unfortunately it was too late as Magnus had gone insane and the Thousand Sons had turned to Chaos and brought their legion to the banner of Horus.  {{Fn|1e}}

====Fate====
At the conclusion of operations on Prospero, Hawser was classified as an unknown future threat to the Space Wolves and the Imperium. While they recognized his innocence and their respect for him they could not allow him to continue as an active member of the Legion. As such, he was placed in permanent stasis in the depths of the [[Fang]] where the dreadnoughts such as [[Cormek Dod]] are reserved to be awoken by future generations of Wolves to recall the accounts of the Heresy and learn from them.{{Fn|1f}}

===Canonical Conflict===
The [[Prospero Burns]] novel gives an account where Kasper severs [[Bjorn|Bjorn's]] lower arm during the Battle of Prospero to prevent the spread of maleficarum.{{Fn|1f}} This differs from another tale stating that his hand was corrupted by psychic feedback from a sorcerer of the Thousand Sons he had just slain. As the corruption crept up along his arm, Chief [[Custodian]] [[Constantin Valdor]] cut it off, saving Bjorn.{{Fn|2}}

===Trivia===
{{trivia}}

*The name ''Kasper Ansbach Hawser'' presumably is inspired by the real world mystery of [[Wikipedia:Kaspar Hauser|Kaspar Hauser]]. He was an individual who seemingly appeared out of nowhere in [[Wikipedia:Ansbach|Ansbach]] and was eventually murdered in said city. [https://youtu.be/_Gad1odrN0E?si=o0ggJu-mUlAnYsux&t=2811 In an podcast with Mira Manga,] [[Dan Abnett]] confirms this. He goes on to compare the themes of ""a character who came out of nowhere" and "being completely oblivious and having lost their short-term memory. Being unable to rely on such things." This also ties into Dan's medical diagnosis of epilepsy while writing ''Prospero Burns''.
*''Ahmad Ibn Rustah'' was a [[Wikipedia:Ahmad_ibn_Rustah|10th century Persian explorer]] who - amongst other things - travelled with and wrote about the [[Wikipedia:Rus' people|Rus' people]].

'''Katerina Moriana''', who went by '''Katt''', was a [[Psyker]] who was a citizen of [[Calth]] when the [[Word Bearers]] [[Battle for Calth|attacked]] the world, during the [[Horus Heresy]]. As the invasion raged, Katt soon joined a small group of Imperials who escaped with the [[Perpetual]] [[Ollanius Persson]], into a [[Warp Rift]] he created.{{Fn|1a}}

She is one of several figures tied into the origins of the mysterious [[Moriana]].{{Fn|5}}

===History===
This began a journey through time and space, as [[Ollanius Persson]] tried to reach [[Terra]] before the traitorous [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]] could kill the [[Emperor]]. In order to do so, Persson had to use a [[Athame]] ritual blade to create numerous temporary [[Warp Rift]]s, to travel through. However soon afterwards, the group began to be pursued by a [[Daemon]] who sought to stop them before they reached Terra. No matter how many Warp Rifts they escaped into, the Daemon was able to track the group down and was always close behind them. This led Katt to discover she had [[Psychic]] abilities, as she was able to determine the length of time it would take before the Daemon reached them{{Fn|1a}}. While Katt's abilities caused some, like [[Hebet Zybes]], to be wary of her{{Fn|1b}}, Persson fully trusted her and relied on her to aid him. So much so, that as they neared Terra, Persson wondered if the group's journey would have been as successful, if they could not have relied on Katt's psychic powers.{{Fn|1a}}   

Katt survived the journey to Terra and the clutches of the [[Emperor's Children]] in the dream-garden known as Paradise. Along with [[John Grammaticus]], she was disdainful of the presence of [[Actaea]] and her [[Alpha Legion]] protector.{{Fn|1d}} Journeying with the group, Katt displayed formidable psychic abilities when their aircraft was engaged by traitor fire over the [[Imperial Palace]].{{Fn|2a}} However in the end their [[Arvus Lighter]] was shot down, and Katt along with the others were escorted by "[[Ingo Pech|Alpharius]]" into the tunnels leading to the [[Sanctum Imperialis]].{{Fn|2b}}

Katt accompanied the group into the [[Imperial Dungeon]], eventually using her powers with the help of John Grammaticus to prove Actaea was not out to help Horus win the war.{{Fn|3a}} The group eventually reached the [[Golden Throne]] alongside the other "[[Argonauts]]", but discovering that the Emperor had gone to fight Horus aboard the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''.{{Fn|3b}}

As the group continued on their quest, they were confronted by [[Erebus]] on the walls of the [[Imperial Palace]]. During the subsequent fight most of the group were slain, culminating in a massive psychic battle between Actaea and Erebus. The psychic blast unleashed by Actaea caused the wall they were standing on to collapse, burying them both in rubble.{{Fn|4a}} As Actaea lay beneath the rubble, surviving only due to her [[Perpetual]] nature, she felt the last gasps of pained life escape from Kat.{{Fn|4b}}

Actaea later discovered that her and Kat's minds had melded together during their mutual deaths, and she takes on her name in the aftermath.{{Fn|5}}
